Potential Cognition AI Round Would Raise $2B-Plus at $75B Valuation
Published
November 20, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Key Points Cognition is discussing a $75 billion round that would far exceed its $48 billion…
View more
Cognition is discussing a $75 billion round that would far exceed its $48 billion September valuation.
Devin's run-rate revenue climbed from $492 million in May to almost $900 million by September.
Cognition positions itself as an independent agent lab free to combine models rather than rely on one provider.
Bloomberg News reported on November 20, 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that Cognition AI was discussing a new funding round at a $75 billion valuation and considering raising $2 billion or more, in an account carried by Reuters . The talks were ongoing and the details could change.
The report described a potential financing rather than a completed investment. Cognition did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment.
Valuation Gap to Completed 2026 Rounds
Cognition announced its Series E on September 8, 2026 , raising more than $2 billion at a $48 billion valuation. New investors Andreessen Horowitz and Accel led the round, joined by existing backers Founders Fund, General Catalyst and Avenir. The proposed figure is $27 billion higher than that completed valuation, calculated as the difference between the two stated valuations.
The earlier May 27, 2026 financing raised more than $1 billion at a $26 billion valuation and was led by Lux Capital, General Catalyst and 8VC. The completed May and September rounds provide reference points for the new report, while the latest terms remain under negotiation.
Devin Adoption and Reported Revenue Growth
Reuters describes Cognition’s autonomous software-engineering agents as able to handle code planning, writing, testing and deployment with limited human intervention. Devin is Cognition’s product for this work.
Cognition’s own disclosures report run-rate revenue growth from $492 million in May to almost $900 million by September, alongside enterprise usage growth of more than tenfold between the start of 2026 and the May announcement. The revenue increase is roughly $400 million, calculated from the two reported run-rate figures.
Cognition says Devin is used by engineering teams at NVIDIA, GE Aerospace, Citi, Mercedes-Benz and Modal, spanning chip design, aviation, financial services, automotive and AI infrastructure. Devin Auto-Triage can handle an initial incident investigation, Devin Security Swarm identifies and prioritizes vulnerabilities, and Devin Automations can begin tasks in response to activity in Slack, GitHub, Linear and other systems without requiring a separate chat for each task.
The September announcement also said Cognition had opened offices in Washington, D.C., Tokyo, Singapore, London, São Paulo and Madrid during the preceding year, alongside its existing San Francisco, New York and Austin hubs. The office expansion accompanied the company’s reported revenue growth and broader customer adoption.
Cognition also describes itself as an independent agent lab that can select and combine models for particular tasks, including its own, so customers are not confined to a single provider. That approach makes model choice part of Devin’s product design as the company expands into incident response, security and event-triggered automation.

articles.title: “This Is Not a Question of Business”: Mark Walter’s Reported Sparks Sale Raises Questions Over $705 Million Price Tag
articles.snippet: “This Is Not a Question of Business”: Mark Walter’s Reported Sparks Sale Raises Questions Over $705 Million Price Tag EssentiallySports
articles.text:
The world’s most expensive garage sale continues. Mark Walter is reportedly close to offloading another major franchise as he continues to dismantle pieces of his global sports portfolio at record-shattering prices. The billionaire sports executive has managed to flip the Los Angeles Lakers, Chelsea FC, and RC Strasbourg. Now it’s the turn of the Los Angeles Sparks, a WNBA team. According to Sportico , Walter, who bought the Los Angeles Sparks for $10 million in 2014 alongside an ownership group that included Lakers legend Magic Johnson, is nearing a record-shattering deal to sell the WNBA franchise to San Diego Padres owners José E. Feliciano and his wife, Kwanza Jones. Just like with the Lakers, he stands to earn a neat profit from the Sparks too, which had Pablo Torre’s Spidey Senses tingling.
Watch What’s Trending Now!
Note: While early reports and initial reactions, including those from Pablo Torre, cited a $750 million figure, Sportico subsequently clarified that the actual sale price is $705 million, still more than double the previous WNBA record of $300 million, set when Houston Rockets owner Tilman Fertitta purchased the Connecticut Sun in March.
ADVERTISEMENT
Even at the corrected $705 million mark, the valuation represents roughly 23 times the Sparks’ estimated 2026 revenue, marking the highest revenue multiple for a major U.S. sports franchise sale since 2022 and surpassing Walter’s pending $12.5 billion Los Angeles Lakers sale at 20x revenue.
On Pardon the Interruption , Frank Isola and Pablo Torre dissected both the staggering price tag and the broader legal pressures surrounding Walter, who is facing federal investigations over alleged self-dealing and faulty disclosures tied to his insurance companies.
ADVERTISEMENT
Isola kicked off the segment by framing the astronomical valuation against the WNBA’s rapid financial climb before asking Torre where the real story lies.
“Sportico reports that Dodgers and outgoing Lakers owner Mark Walter is close to selling the WNBA Sparks to the owners of baseball’s Padres. For, get this—750 million. That’s 300 million higher than the New York Liberty were valued for a minority investment last year. All right, Pablo, are you more focused on Walter’s potential sale or the reported price tag?” Isola asked.
ADVERTISEMENT
Torre immediately argued that the eye-popping number and Walter’s urgent sell-off cannot be separated.
“I think it’s the same story, and I’ve been investigating this on my show, Pablo Torre Finds Out. One of the things, Frank, to know about the business… so annual revenue for the Sparks is about 25 to $28 million. Doing the math, we’re looking at more than 25x revenue. When you say, ‘Okay, they’re going to go for 750 million,’ that is beyond AI company-level absurdity, right? We’re now untethered from reality. This is not a question of business. This is a question of Mark Walter needing to sell his sports teams, as he is under federal investigation for these faulty disclosures around his insurance companies and alleged self-dealing stuff that’s come up in class-action lawsuits.”

articles.text:
Sellas , Life
Sellas Life Sciences: Placement Closes at $172.5 Million as REGAL Data Sit Alongside a Bigger Share Count
Published on 11/22/2026 at 17:11 | Editorial boerse-global.de
Sellas closed its $172.5M placement at $13.00 per share, with shares down 8.1%, as investors weigh dilution against REGAL Phase III survival data.
Sellas Life Sciences Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Sellas Life Sciences wrapped up its public share placement on Friday, and the market's response was swift: the stock closed 8.1% lower as investors weighed the cost of fresh equity against the clinical progress the company has been touting. The offering, priced at $13.00 per share on November 18, ultimately comprised 13,269,231 shares — a figure that includes the full exercise of the underwriters' overallotment option — for gross proceeds of $172.5 million.
That "gross" qualifier matters. Placement discounts, commissions and other offering expenses still come out of the headline number, so the actual cash inflow will land below the stated total. Sellas had originally targeted $150.0 million in gross proceeds; the bankers' 30-day option to buy additional shares, exercised in full, is what pushed the transaction to its final size.
Two Questions, Not One
The placement and the clinical program answer entirely different questions, and conflating them serves neither. A capital raise speaks to the balance sheet; a Phase III readout speaks to the science. Treating a financing decision as a seal of approval for the entire investment case is a shortcut that skips the hard part.
On the balance-sheet side, the picture is straightforward. The raise bolsters Sellas's capital base, but it does so by issuing new stock — meaning existing holders absorb dilution of their stakes. That tension, rather than any single headline, is the more useful frame for assessing where the company stands.
Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Sellas Life Sciences?
What the Trial Showed
The medical story centers on REGAL, the Phase III study of galinpepimut-S in acute myeloid leukemia. Sellas reported last week that the trial met its primary endpoint of overall survival. Median overall survival came in at 24.0 months, against 14.7 months for patients on the best available therapy — a 41% reduction in the risk of death, according to the company. The hazard ratio was 0.59, with a p-value of 0.035.
Those numbers are the clinical core of the story. The financing step neither replaces them nor diminishes them. What investors need to hold separately is the strength of the evidence and the status of the regulatory path.
The Filing Is Still Ahead
Sellas said it plans to discuss an accelerated submission strategy with the FDA and is preparing a biologics license application for the first half of 2027. Those remain intentions, not achievements — the endpoint has been met, but the conversations and the application preparations are still to come.
Sellas Life Sciences at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now.
The third-quarter figures, released November 12, add another layer. Sellas posted a net loss of $10.1 million for Q3 2026, wider than the $6.8 million shortfall in the same period a year earlier. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $134.7 million at quarter-end.
What Investors Are Left to Weigh

Long bootstrapped, Redbrick Offices raises Rs 630 crore led by Abakkus and India SME Investments
Sumit Vishwakarma
21 Nov 2026
19:35
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Mumbai-based managed workspace provider Redbrick Offices has secured about Rs 630 crore ($72 million), including conditional commitments, in equity across its Series A and Series A1 rounds, led by India SME Investments and Abakkus Asset Manager.
Advertisment
The funding is mostly a primary infusion, with a smaller secondary component through which some existing shareholders sold shares.
India SME Investments led the Series A round in March 2026. The Series A1 round was led more recently by Abakkus's Four2Eight Opportunities Fund, and India SME Investments made a follow-on investment in it.
Evolvence Equity Partners, IIFL Capital Asset Management and UTI Alternatives were among the other investors in the extended round. UTI Alternatives had earlier invested in Redbrick through a structured convertible debenture issuance in March 2025.
Ladderup Corporate Advisory and IIFL Capital Services were financial advisers to the company, and Rajani Associates was its legal adviser.
What the capital is for
Redbrick plans to expand its managed office portfolio from about 6.5 million sq ft to more than 10 million sq ft over the next 18 to 24 months, an increase of roughly 54%.
It will also put money into technology infrastructure, design and service delivery, as it goes after workspace requirements from large enterprises and global capability centres (GCCs). The company said it is open to strategic partnerships and acquisitions that fit its growth plans.
“ This funding validates our consistent focus on improving unit economics as well as demand backed sustainable profitable growth strategy. The equity raise will strengthen our capabilities, accelerate innovation, and renew our focus on addressing the customer's requirements while acting as a long-term partner to large real estate developers, ” said Ayush Goenka, chairman and MD of Redbrick Offices.
“ As flexible asset-light corporate spaces become a core component of real estate strategy for multinationals and GCCs in India, Redbrick is positioned to capture massive market share, ” said Ankit Aggarwal, senior vice president and senior fund manager, private equity at Abakkus. He added Redbrick as a capital-efficient business that has scaled while staying profitable.
“ Our decision to back Redbrick in March 2026, amid peak global uncertainties, was anchored in our belief in Ayush and the management team's track record of building a sizeable business in a bootstrapped manner, with a clear focus on profitable growth, ” said Mitin Jain, founder and managing partner of India SME Investments. He added that the participation of other institutional investors in the latest round reinforced that view.
What Redbrick does
Redbrick runs more than 70 centres across eight cities, with over 1.15 lakh seats. It builds Grade-A offices to a client's specifications and provides facilities management and hospitality-led services through a wholly owned subsidiary, Snow White Technologies & Services Private Limited.
Its clients include GCCs, Fortune 500 companies, large enterprises, BFSI firms and US-based multinationals.
The company counts brands such as Amazon, Salesforce, Flipkart, Cisco, HDFC, Lenovo, Panasonic, BASF and Roche among its clients, with plans to expand into Chennai and Kolkata during 2026-27.

articles.title: 13-Year-Old Hyderabad Student Launches KIKA AI, Secures Seed Funding for AI Platform
articles.snippet: 13-Year-Old Hyderabad Student Launches KIKA AI, Secures Seed Funding for AI Platform https://ascendants.in/
articles.text:
13-Year-Old Hyderabad Student Launches KIKA AI, Secures Seed Funding for AI Platform
Om Singh
| November 21 | The Ascendants
Share
A 13-year-old student from Hyderabad has launched KIKA AI , an artificial intelligence platform designed to help school students and young creators build projects using multiple AI agents and models through a single interface.
Kiyan, a Class 9 student at Delhi Public School, Hyderabad, founded the platform after finding conventional developer tools too technically complex. Instead of navigating complicated setups, he wanted to create a simpler environment where users could focus on building projects and using AI.
The platform has also received seed funding from Tasleem Arif, a technology leader with more than two decades of experience in the smartphone, software and embedded systems industries.
KIKA AI: How the idea took shape
Kiyan started developing KIKA AI on July 13, 2026. The platform reached a working product in approximately 11 weeks.
The idea emerged from his own experience of working with developer tools. He found that technical requirements and complex configurations could make it difficult for beginners to turn their ideas into working projects.
KIKA AI was developed to address this challenge by bringing different AI agents and models together in one place. The platform aims to reduce the technical barriers that students and young creators often encounter when experimenting with artificial intelligence.
Features and target audience
KIKA AI describes itself as an AI-native platform, with a unified interface that allows users to access multiple AI agents and models.
Its primary audience includes school students, particularly those interested in using artificial intelligence for projects and creative work without having to navigate conventional developer environments.
The platform’s broader objective is to make AI tools more accessible to students across India.
According to figures cited at the launch, India has approximately 9 crore students studying in Classes 8 to 12. This represents nearly 6% of the country’s population and forms the potential audience KIKA AI hopes to reach.
KIKA AI receives seed funding
KIKA AI has received seed funding from Tasleem Arif, who has spent more than two decades working across the smartphone, software and embedded systems industries.
Commenting on Kiyan’s initiative, Arif said the young founder demonstrated the ability to identify a real problem and work towards developing a solution.
Prashant Singh, CEO of ONGC Green Limited, also praised the initiative, describing it as “truly inspiring”.
The funding provides early support for the student-led venture as it works towards its goal of making artificial intelligence easier to use for younger audiences.
What is next for the student-led AI venture?
KIKA AI enters the market with a focus on school students at a time when artificial intelligence tools are increasingly being used for learning and academic projects.
However, the platform has not yet disclosed its pricing structure or the number of users it has onboarded. Further details about its commercial model and user adoption remain unavailable.
Meanwhile, Kiyan continues to pursue his Class 9 studies alongside developing the platform, balancing his academic responsibilities with building an AI-focused venture.
